title: Microstarter templates: ergonomic SDK samples (Next.js, FastAPI, Go HTTP, CLI) with retries + streaming patterns
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Ship a set of small, opinionated starter templates (Next.js, FastAPI, Go HTTP server, and a CLI) that demonstrate best-practice usage patterns for Redwood SDKs covering: ergonomic streaming consumption, robust retry strategies (idempotency keys, jittered backoff), client-side backpressure for prefix/KV cache friendly workloads, and minimal production-grade telemetry hooks. These microstarters should be copy-paste ready for product teams and referenced from the docs quickstart. Deliverables: 4 repo-style sample folders with README, a short walkthrough doc, and a single example integration test per sample. Focus on: - idiomatic TypeScript/React usage for streaming in Next.js with progressive UI updates and cancellation - FastAPI server example showing streaming server->client SSE for token-by-token and a server-side retry middleware - Go HTTP example implementing continuous read of chunked responses, graceful shutdown, and connection pooling best practices - CLI that demonstrates resumable streaming with checkpointed KV-cache reuse and configurable retry policies. Non-goals: full-featured starter app, multi-region infra setup.
acceptance_criteria: Each template includes a short README with setup + run instructions (macOS/Linux) and a one-paragraph explanation of trade-offs
Next.js sample demonstrates streaming tokens into a progressive message component and supports cancel + resume in the browser
FastAPI sample shows server-side streaming response + retry middleware that respects idempotency keys and logs retry metrics
Go HTTP sample includes connection pooling config and an example of reading chunked responses robustly
CLI sample demonstrates resumable streams (local checkpoint file) and exposes backoff/retry knobs via flags
All samples include example telemetry hooks (span id, request id) and link to a field test dashboard
One integration test per sample validates basic end-to-end behavior using local mock runtime (unit/ci friendly)
PR merged with code owners approvals and a docs quickstart link updated
implementation_notes: Design decisions: - Provide a minimal wrapper around the raw streaming API that normalizes chunk boundaries into complete tokens/messages to simplify UI code. - Use idempotency keys for POSTs that trigger long-running generation; store key->checkpoint mapping for CLI resume. - For retries: default to exponential backoff with full jitter, cap retries at 5, and surface retry counts via response headers. - Streaming cancellation should close the HTTP body correctly and call SDK cancel token to unblock server-side resources. - Telemetry: attach request_id + span_id to every request; emit an example trace to the sample dashboard. - Use environment flag REDWOOD_API_MOCK=true for CI-friendly mocks.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly opinionated patterns could conflict with some customers' infra. Mitigation: keep templates tiny and clearly document trade-offs.
Risk: Streaming cancellation semantics differ across runtimes (browser vs Go). Mitigation: implement and document explicit cancel() + close() sequences and provide helper utilities in each sample.
Risk: Retry idempotency misuse. Mitigation: show both idempotent and non-idempotent example flows and recommend idempotency-key approach for non-idempotent actions.
